verdict.rationale: Antigravity CLI documents a sandbox mode that blocks sensitive files like ~/.ssh and .env and hides anything not explicitly mounted, and Git worktrees plus Deny/Ask/Allow permissions and Project folder boundaries further isolate what agents can reach. This isolates the agent's local filesystem, but nothing describes a dedicated test environment separated from production data or services. Hands-on reports of the agent reading .env via prompt injection and deleting a drive in auto-execute mode concern the IDE rather than the documented CLI sandbox, so they lower confidence rather than dispute the claim. Missing for 10: an explicit sandbox or staging environment for data and services separate from production, in-depth sandbox documentation beyond one line, independent confirmation that the sandbox isolation holds.
